items.title: Charlie Cordilla Interview, 1952-05-17
items.q: Did you ever play with Emmett? Yes, I played with him.

ctx.x: the drums do. Now let's go back to Union's Rhythm King session. Yeah. Because those are historical records. Rap is on quite a number of them. Yeah. And then he suddenly disappears. And that was the result of that deal with Santo. That's right. That one particular record, which was one side was She's Crying For Me Blues. It was Santo's number. And I'll never forget that morning. We went up there to cut the racket and Rapolo sent his brother up there, Nick, to tell me that I better not play his solo. He had a…

Well, I think him and Big Spine are back. Is that so? Did you ever play with Big? No, I've never played with him. Did you ever hear him? Yeah, yeah, yeah. They always said that he tried to imitate Emmett. Is that right? Yeah, that's right. That's right. Emmett was quite young, didn't he? He did, yes. Did you ever play with Emmett? Yes, I played with him. Which band, any particular? Well, no, I'll tell you, quite a few times he played some extra jobs that Abby Brunner couldn't make out at the halfway house. By the…
